title: Grateful Dead Live at Roosevelt Stadium on 1973-08-01

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of the legendary 8/1/73 Jerry Garcia birthday show delivers a solid performance with a standout Dark Star → El Paso → Eyes → Morning Dew sequence, despite minor mix quirks.
ai_review.review: The SIRMick sound‑board source captures the energy of Jerry’s 31st birthday gig at Roosevelt Stadium, with reviewers raving about the second‑set “meat” sequence and the high‑octane Big River.  The audio is generally clean but a few listeners note instrument balance issues on Bird Song and recommend an EQ tweak.  Overall the show is considered a keeper, especially for fans of the 1973 era.

ai_rating.rationale: Five reviews are uniformly enthusiastic (average 4.6★) and highlight strong musical moments; technical comments note only minor mix issues, yielding a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear SIRMick sound‑board tape; occasional instrument balance hiccup on Bird Song and recommendation to use EQ for optimal playback.

standout_songs: Dark Star > El Paso > Eyes > Morning Dew
Sugar Magnolia > Good Lovin' (GDTRFB) > One More Saturday Night
poor_songs: First set overall considered uneven by some reviewers
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is mixed and never fully turns the corner, but the second set builds strong momentum with a classic meat sequence that lifts the entire concert.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for solid, professional playing; unique solo notes and energetic lead throughout especially on Dark Star and Big River.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned for vocal delivery on Sugar Magnolia, channeling Donna’s spirit; generally supportive rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux receives kudos for piano nudging on Sugaree and high energy throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann highlighted as possibly “the best drummer ever,” with tight cymbal work and driving beats during the meat sequence.
